args.body:
Hi Dora! Thanks for accepting the Slack invite — I'm Emma Johnson from Blue Sparrow Tech. I took a look at your personal website (www.dora-website.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- It's clean and straightforward — the page loads fast and tells me exactly who it belongs to.
- Having your email right on the page makes it easy for people to reach you.

Where I'd suggest improving:
- The site is very sparse right now. A short intro about who you are and what you do would give visitors an instant sense of your work.
- Consider adding a few sections that show more of you — for example, projects you've worked on, a brief bio, or links to your other profiles.
- A bit of visual personality (some color, a photo, or a simple layout with headings) would make it feel more like a home on the web than a placeholder.
- If you write or post anything regularly, a small blog or news section would be a great addition.

Overall it's a nice, no-fuss starting point — just a little more content and personality would take it a long way. Happy to share more specific ideas if you're interested!

Best,
Emma Johnson
Blue Sparrow Tech

Hi Eve! I'm Emma Johnson from Blue Sparrow Tech. I had a look at your blog (www.eve-blog.com) and wanted to send you some feedback.

What I liked:
- The blog has a clear, personal voice right from the start.
- Hiking is a fantastic hobby to write about — it's the kind of topic people genuinely enjoy reading, and it gives the blog a warm, outdoorsy identity.
- The page is simple and easy to read, which is a real plus.

Where I'd suggest improving:
- Since hiking is your passion, I'd love to see it come through in the content — trail write-ups, gear reviews, route guides, or photo essays would all be great starting points.
- Adding a short "About" section would help readers get to know you before they dive into posts.
- A simple archive or list of recent posts would make it easier for visitors to find their way around, especially as the blog grows.
- Some visual polish — a header image, trail photos, or a consistent color theme — would really complement the subject matter.
- If you travel often, a map or list of the places you've hiked could become a signature feature of the blog.

Overall, it's a promising start with a topic that has real appeal. I'd love to see it grow into a space that reflects your enthusiasm for the outdoors!

Best,
Emma Johnson
Blue Sparrow Tech
